findings.title: Retain the existing public CSV and TSV entry points
findings.evidence: The diff removes the public csv/1 and tsv/1 functions and only adds encode/2. Existing calls Export.csv([1, 2]) and Export.tsv([1, 2]) now raise UndefinedFunctionError instead of returning encoded text; this was reproduced with the current module. The supplied repository contains no migration or compatibility contract permitting removal.
findings.correction: Keep csv/1 and tsv/1 as public compatibility functions delegating to encode/2, or supply and validate an explicitly breaking migration for every consumer.

missing_context: No callers, compatibility policy, or API migration documentation are supplied, so downstream usage and whether a breaking release was intended cannot be established.
tests_run: Elixir probe: encode/2 returns comma-separated and tab-separated text; calls to the prior csv/1 and tsv/1 exports both raise UndefinedFunctionError.
Elixir probe: timeout retry with one stable operation_id returns success and stores exactly one shipment; replay deduplicates and a conflicting order preserves the key_conflict error.

findings.title: Keep the capacity check and decrement in one atomic operation
findings.evidence: reserve/1 now reads capacity and decrements it in separate Agent calls. With capacity 1, two concurrent requests can both read 1, both return :ok, and leave capacity -1, violating the module's explicit concurrent-reservation limit. A probe queued both reads while the Agent was suspended, then resumed it, and reproduced [:ok, :ok] with -1 remaining.
findings.correction: Restore a single Agent.get_and_update/2 that checks the count and decrements it atomically; add a concurrent capacity-one regression test.

tests_run: Deterministic Elixir concurrency probe: suspend a capacity-one Agent, queue both reservation reads, resume, and observe two successful reservations and remaining capacity -1.

findings.title: Reuse the durable operation ID when retrying a timed-out shipment
findings.evidence: The supplied Shipping.create/3 commits a new key before returning {:error, :timeout}; only reuse of that key deduplicates the operation. Retrying with make_ref() submits the same order under another key. An ordinary first call to run/2 stored two shipments for one order and still returned {:error, :timeout}.
findings.correction: Pass order.operation_id on the retry, preserving the same order payload, and assert that a lost initial reply followed by retry stores exactly one shipment.

tests_run: Elixir probe using the supplied Shipping Agent: one run/2 call returned {:error, :timeout} and stored two identical orders under distinct keys.

Deterministic Elixir concurrency probe: queue two availability checks against a suspended capacity-one pool, resume, and verify exactly one :ok, one :full, and zero remaining capacity; further reservation returns :full.

findings.title: Assert the counter's public behavior instead of its private Agent state
findings.evidence: The module explicitly defines only start_link/0, add/2, and value/1 as public behavior, and the preceding assertion already verifies the claimed value change. The new :sys.get_state/1 equality additionally freezes the private map representation. In an isolated copy, changing only storage from %{value: n} to n preserved public start/add/value behavior but made the unchanged test fail exclusively on this new assertion.
findings.correction: Remove the private-state assertion and retain the public value/1 assertion; add further public-operation sequences only for behavior that needs coverage.

tests_run: Isolated integer-state Counter probe preserved start_link/0, add/2, and value/1 across zero, positive, and negative values.
Unchanged counter test against the isolated equivalent representation: failed only at the new :sys.get_state/1 assertion.

missing_context: The adapter implementation and send_order/2 contract are absent. A timeout may mean no delivery or successful delivery with a lost reply; it is unknown whether repeated order.id values deduplicate atomically and for the required duration.
No callers, retry policy, or tests establish whether retrying delivery on timeout is permitted.

Database schema and migrations are absent, so the required unique index/constraint for accounts.email and its name cannot be verified. unsafe_validate_unique/3 alone cannot establish concurrent uniqueness; unique_constraint/2 is correct only with the corresponding database enforcement.
App.Repo, the Ecto dependency/version, and runnable test configuration are absent; no supplied stand-in allows exercising the insert or concurrent-registration contract.

findings.title: Keep Worklist state access inside its owning module
findings.evidence: Worklist explicitly declares its state private, but the new Dashboard.pending_count/1 and Export.pending_ids/1 both call Agent.get/2 and assume a %{pending: list} representation; Export also knows that the list is stored in reverse insertion order. Changing the queue representation while preserving start_link/add/take now requires synchronized changes in both unrelated consumers or their reads fail/return the wrong order. This is concrete representation coupling introduced by the new files, not a current count mismatch.
findings.correction: Expose pending_count/1 and pending_ids/1 (with explicit ordering) from Worklist and have Dashboard and Export call those public operations so storage knowledge stays with the owner.

tests_run: Elixir observer probe passed for empty queue, two additions, and one take; confirmed current counts and insertion-order exported IDs.

findings.title: Keep invoice completion and trial activation as separate domain operations
findings.evidence: The only two consumers always pass opposite fixed triples of flags: Billing requires an invoice with tax and payment, while Trials requires a duration with no payment. Completion.run/2 combines their different input/output contracts, tests the trial flag twice, and exposes independent include_tax/collect switches with no supplied caller needing those variations. Understanding or changing either small policy now requires tracing a generic options layer and guarding the unrelated domain's branches; the original separate map constructors express the complete supported behavior directly. The actual callers still produce correct results.
findings.correction: Restore the small domain-specific implementations in Billing.complete/1 and Trials.activate/1, or extract only a genuinely shared operation once one exists.

tests_run: Elixir probe: taxed invoice, zero-value invoice, and unpaid trial all match the documented current caller behavior.
Unchanged test in an isolated copy with pay/2 mutated to call the synchronous gateway twice: failed at refute_received, demonstrating that the new assertion detects a duplicate charge.
Supplied protocol test: 1 passed, covering atom and tuple v1 request forms.
Elixir probe: new Dashboard.status/1 returns the documented {:ready, 4} snapshot; retained tuple v1 request returns the same result.
